content.text: I'll create a channel beam with the specified dimensions. Let me first calculate the necessary coordinates for creating this geometry using blocks.

input.PythonCode:
# Channel beam dimensions
width = 70  # mm
height = 40  # mm
length = 450  # mm
wall_thickness = 5  # mm

# Calculate the coordinates for the blocks
# We'll create one main block and subtract the inner cavity

# Main block (outer dimensions)
main_block = {
    'x': 0,
    'y': 0,
    'z': 0,
    'x_size': width,
    'y_size': height,
    'z_size': length
}

# Inner cavity block (to be subtracted)
# The cavity starts at wall_thickness from the sides and bottom
# It's open on top, so it goes all the way to the top
cavity_block = {
    'x': wall_thickness,
    'y': 0,  # Open on top, so cavity starts from the bottom
    'z': wall_thickness,
    'x_size': width - 2 * wall_thickness,  # 70 - 10 = 60mm
    'y_size': height,  # Full height since it's open on top
    'z_size': length - 2 * wall_thickness  # 450 - 10 = 440mm
}

print("Main block dimensions:")
print(f"Position: ({main_block['x']}, {main_block['y']}, {main_block['z']})")
print(f"Size: {main_block['x_size']} x {main_block['y_size']} x {main_block['z_size']}")
print()
print("Cavity block dimensions:")
print(f"Position: ({cavity_block['x']}, {cavity_block['y']}, {cavity_block['z']})")
print(f"Size: {cavity_block['x_size']} x {cavity_block['y_size']} x {cavity_block['z_size']}")
